title: The overlap needs material too
hook: A 2cm overlap repeats along a 20cm edge. Where does its area go?

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Include a seam or overlap strip in area requirements.

misconception: Hidden overlap does not contribute to material area.
objective: Include a seam or overlap strip in area requirements.

claims.text: An ideal paper rectangle is 20cm long. Its 30cm width needs a further 2cm overlap. Scaled model; ideal paper; overlap=2cm; no cutting guidance.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Width=30cm, A=640cm² and B=600cm². The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",["+","x",2],20]; B=["*","x",20]; x denotes Width. At x=30, A=640, B=600; recall at x=45: B=900. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: The extra strip has width two and length twenty, so it adds forty square centimetres. The overlap is material that exists even when it is hidden beneath another layer.

recall.question: An ideal paper rectangle is 20cm long. Its 30cm width needs a further 2cm overlap. Change only Width to 45cm. What is B (No-overlap) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Width=45cm: it gives 900cm². The extra strip has width two and length twenty, so it adds forty square centimetres. The overlap is material that exists even when it is hidden beneath another layer.
